note: Structural import matrix. This is the machine-readable form of the boundaries in docs/COLONIE-BLUEPRINT.md section 7. Every deny rule here has zero violations today and the baseline is empty, so any crossing is a new one; the rules that earlier drafts proposed and this measurement rejected (features importing server/routes/table.ts and server/harness/http.ts) are recorded in docs/structure/README.md. A path entry matches the path itself or any path that starts with it; an empty entry matches everything.

deny.why: index.ts is the composition root and the process entry point; anything importing it would make the boot order load-bearing again, which is what the restructure removed.
shared/ is compiled into both the server and the renderer; reaching into either side makes it a two-sided module with a build dependency nobody declared.
the server does not run in the renderer; an import here would only ever work in the dev build where both trees exist on disk.
the renderer talks to the server over HTTP/SSE. Importing server internals would pull SQL, credentials and provider code into the browser bundle.

harness/ is the composition and startup layer: a feature that imports it cannot be tested or read without booting the server. routes/ is the adapter layer that depends on features, never the reverse. Two modules are the sanctioned exception: routes/table.ts is the shared route contract the blueprint tells feature-owned adapters to reuse, and harness/http.ts is a shared request/response helper that carries no boot order.
